analysis: Market context: S&P 500 has rebounded from early-2025 tariff-shock lows but remains in a mixed-to-recovering trend — many quality names sit 10-25% below their 200-day SMAs, which is exactly the basing-zone opportunity the strategy targets. The screened list is rich with quality businesses, but only a handful combine (a) genuinely attractive forward valuations, (b) basing patterns in the lower half of their 52-week range, and (c) SMA50 slopes that have stopped deteriorating. Three names stand out with asymmetric setups: ROP (quality serial acquirer at fwd P/E ~15, only 16% off the 52w low, uptrend basing), MSFT (best-in-class franchise at fwd P/E ~21 — reasonable for 18%+ revenue growth — 30% of range, basing near SMA50), and CI (Cigna at fwd P/E ~8, massive FCF yield, effectively flat vs SMA50 and SMA200, deeply undervalued vs healthcare peers). Combined, these three consume ~75% of equity with each position sized so that a full stop-out costs ~1.1-1.2% of total equity. 25% cash buffer retained. No forced trades on lower-conviction names like COIN (revenue shrinking), TRMB (PEG 3.84 + negative revenue growth), or PAYX (SMA50 slope -2.7%, near 52w lows with downward momentum). Confidence in compounding toward ~1% weekly is moderate — these are position/LTCG trades, not swing trades, so weekly progress will be lumpy.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $355 or better; accept fills up to $360 on continuation. Ideal entry on any intraday dip toward the 20-day EMA (~$353). Do not chase above $365.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Roper is a capital-light, asset-light serial acquirer of niche vertical-software businesses — the kind of compounding machine that earns a premium multiple. Forward P/E of ~15x is the cheapest it has traded in years; the market is pricing in macro fear, not business deterioration. FCF of $2.2B on a $36B market cap = ~6% FCF yield. Revenue growing 11%, operating margins 27%, and the Vertafore/Procore-style recurring software model insulates it from tariff risk. TECHNICAL: Price sits at only 16% of the 52-week range ($314-$578), well within the basing zone. Trend is classified UPTREND (basing) with SMA50 slope turning positive (+0.9% over 20 days) after a prolonged downtrend. Currently within 0.7% of SMA50 — this is the cleanest Stage 1-to-2 transition setup on the entire list. ATR is a manageable 2.6%, allowing a tight 1.73x-ATR stop.
trades.exit_plan: Exit thesis break: ROP completes a large acquisition at a clearly value-destructive price, or quarterly FCF growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters. Time stop: reassess if price has not made progress toward $390 within 90 days. Trail stop up to SMA50 once +10% in profit. Consider LTCG extension if still in position at 11 months and thesis intact.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $410 or on a pullback toward the SMA50 (~$397). Do not buy above $420 — that would be chasing extension. Wait for at least one session of consolidation after any gap-up.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Microsoft is the highest-quality franchise on this list and arguably in the entire S&P 500 — 46% operating margins, 34% ROE, $37B FCF, $170B operating cash flow, 18%+ revenue growth driven by Azure cloud and Copilot AI monetization. Forward P/E of ~21x is materially below the 5-year average of ~30x; the market has re-rated it lower on macro/rate fears, not because the business is impaired. The AI infrastructure buildout (OpenAI partnership, Copilot, Azure AI) is a multi-year earnings catalyst that consensus models likely underestimate. TECHNICAL: Currently 30% of the 52-week range ($357-$540), squarely in the lower-half basing zone. Price is 3.6% above SMA50 — not extended. SMA50 slope is slightly negative (-0.7%) but flattening; the pattern is consistent with a base forming before a new leg. At -11.7% below SMA200, there is substantial overhead supply to work through, but the target merely asks for partial recovery to $465 (still -14% below the prior high).
trades.exit_plan: Thesis break: Azure growth decelerates below 25% YoY for two consecutive quarters, or a major AI regulatory event impairs the OpenAI relationship. Time stop: if no progress toward $440 within 120 days, reassess position size. Trail stop to SMA50 once +8% profit. Strong preference to hold past 12 months for LTCG treatment given the compounding thesis.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $274 or better. CI has been consolidating tightly between $260-$285; entry near the lower end of that range with the stop below the base. Acceptable to buy at market if opens near $275.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Cigna (The Cigna Group) is one of the cheapest large-cap quality businesses on the screen. Forward P/E of 8.2x and PEG of 0.84 suggest the market is pricing in near-permanent margin compression that is unlikely to materialize at this level. FCF of $6.9B on a $73B market cap = ~9.5% FCF yield — extraordinary for a company growing revenue 4.6% with 16% ROE and significant buyback capacity. Healthcare is structurally defensive; Cigna's Evernorth pharmacy services segment provides diversification away from pure managed-care uncertainty. The stock has been beaten down on PBM regulatory noise and UnitedHealth sector contagion — not Cigna-specific deterioration. TECHNICAL: Price is at 39% of the 52-week range, classified MIXED/SIDEWAYS basing, currently within 0.5% of its SMA50 and only -1.5% below SMA200 — effectively flat to both moving averages, which is the tightest coil setup in the list. SMA50 slope at -0.3% is nearly flat, suggesting the selling pressure is exhausted. ATR of 2.8% allows a well-placed stop just below the recent consolidation lows.
trades.exit_plan: Thesis break: quarterly earnings show accelerating membership losses in Evernorth or adverse CMS rate decisions materially below guidance. Sector-wide managed-care regulatory action (e.g., PBM legislation passing) would require reassessment. Time stop: if stock cannot reclaim $285 within 60 days, reduce to half size. Target is the mid-range of the 52-week band; consider extending hold toward the prior high ($329) if forward P/E remains below 10x at that point.
